answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer: It’s best to give the body 2‑3 weeks of full recovery before adding new race work.  After a month of light, easy miles you can start a mild 10‑K build in five weeks, but keep the intensity low and watch for any lingering pain or swelling.

new.analysis:
The athlete ran a marathon on Oct 18 and had some quad and calf soreness and a toe blister.  The recent week was mostly easy and the last hard work was the race.  In a recovery phase we keep volume low, focus on 80 % easy sessions, avoid back‑to‑back hard work and watch for any swelling or pain that might worsen.  The plan for the week of Oct 19 – 25 will give 4–5 easy miles spread over the week with a full rest day and a short active recovery on the weekend.  The athlete’s question was how long before they can run again and whether they can target a 10 K in five weeks – the answer is to give 2‑3 weeks of full recovery before adding any race‑specific training, then they can start a light 10‑K build after a month of easy miles.


I will highlight quadriceps soreness, heel blister, sleep quality, HR drift and general recovery progress as flags.

No medical diagnoses are made; any persisting pain or swelling should be checked by a professional.

Plan dates:
Mon Oct 19 – rest
Tue Oct 20 – easy, 4.5 mi, heart rate <150, keep the pace comfortable, helps maintain range.
Wed Oct 21 – easy, 3.5 mi, keep the legs loose, allows extra recovery.
Thu Oct 22 – easy, 4 mi, keep the mileage low, keep heart rate steady.
Fri Oct 23 – rest, allow full recovery.
Sat Oct 24 – easy, 3 mi, short run to keep legs moving.
Sun Oct 25 – easy, 3.5 mi, keep the finish light, finish the week strong.


The answer to the question: wait 2‑3 weeks, then start with easy miles and a mild 10‑K training block a month later.


No safety callouts are required.
